impact_scope.description: The existing meshopt_generateNormals callable changes how its smoothing path normalizes accumulated and per-pass normals, without changing its signature, caller-supplied parameters, configuration, or lifecycle.

evidence: In S0, meshopt_generateNormals already exists with the smoothing parameter and the same caller-visible signature.
H0 contains no call to meshopt_generateNormals, so it does not exercise the existing normal-generation or smoothing path.
In S1, meshopt_generateNormals remains the same callable with the same caller-visible signature and smoothing control.
H0 is unchanged and still contains no call to meshopt_generateNormals; the changed normalization behavior is internal to that omitted callable.

new_harness_obligation.description: S1 requires no new H0 entry point, argument, buffer, configuration, call ordering, or special input construction beyond the direct meshopt_generateNormals call already omitted in S0.
evidence: The meshopt_generateNormals declaration and its parameters are identical across S0 and S1.
The diff only reorganizes normalization within the existing smoothing implementation; callers continue to control it through the pre-existing smoothing argument.

reason: The same public callable and exposure obligation exist on both sides, and H0 omits that callable in both snapshots. Changed internal behavior does not add or aggravate a caller-visible harness obligation.
